title: Highly Parallel Droplet Sample Preparation for Single Cell Proteomics
author: Andrew Leduc
materials: the trypsin is highly viscous, so be sure to run "dip wash" after aspirating, and reduce frequency, voltage, and pulse considerably

if a droplet seems to be shooting off to the side, dabbing the bottom of the tip twice with a kimwipe (damp with ethanol) can really help. If the issue persists, move nozzle to home position, turn on continuous dispensing, and try cleaning tip with an ethanol-dampened kimwipe for ~60 seconds.
Generally higher voltage has helped with DMSO dispensing. Also make sure humidity is not too high when dispensing DMSO, this can cause droplets to stick to the end of nozzle.

If multiplexing reagents are stored in acetonitrile, evaporate off acetonitrile completely in speed vacuum on low heat or lyophilizer. Re-suspend TMT labels in 100% DMSO at a concentration of 1/3 maximum strength. You will need a volume of 25 uL of TMT label (this volume is post 1/3 dilution). This gives enough volume for a retry if there is a failure with the label. Critical: Pipette mix labels vigorously to prevent TMT crystals from forming as these can interfere with label dispensing.

We recommend using the 384 well PCR plate from thermofisher. In order to use this plate to pick up the samples with an ultimate 3000, you will need to purchase the attachment below which raises the plate up a bit. https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/6820.4088#/6820.4088

Practice with the reagents you will be using before starting a prep. Several factors such as humidity, room temperature and the specific nozzle can have large effects on dispensing accuracy. As an example, for dispensing mTRAQ labels, I use DMSO as I found it easiest to work with, however, we have also used Ethanol and IPA for dispensing mTRAQ in the past. This can work well, but, requires you to aspirate air and then ~20 uL of organic solvent prior to aspirating label and dispensing. Some tips that have worked for me: 1) the trypsin is highly viscous, so be sure to run "dip wash" after aspirating, and reduce frequency, voltage, and pulse considerably 2) if a droplet seems to be shooting off to the side, dabbing the bottom of the tip twice with a kimwipe (damp with ethanol) can really help. If the issue persists, move nozzle to home position, turn on continuous dispensing, and try cleaning tip with an ethanol-dampened kimwipe for ~60 seconds. 3) Generally higher voltage has helped with DMSO dispensing. Also make sure humidity is not too high when dispensing DMSO, this can cause droplets to stick to the end of nozzle.

steps.title: Install CellenONE files
steps.instruction: Copy the repository files into the CellenONE directories: Tasks → C:\Users\Scienion AG\CellenONE\Settings\Task, Runs → C:\Users\Scienion AG\CellenONE\Settings\Run, Droplet Layouts → C:\Users\Scienion AG\CellenONE\Pattern. Close and reopen the CellenONE software to verify the files appear in the Run panel, Do task sub‑tab, and as field files.

steps.title: Configure TMT18 droplet layout
steps.instruction: If using the TMT‑18 plex option, set the droplet layout so that each set contains 14 single‑cell spots; the carrier and reference occupy two spots and two additional spots are left empty for isotopic impurities.

steps.title: Create Slides_MetalHolder_copy target
steps.instruction: In the Robot Setup tab, go to Target Sub‑tab, select Slides_MetalHolder, click Duplicate Target, name the copy Slides_MetalHolder_copy, and copy the settings as shown in the reference picture.

steps.title: Create SlidePickup target with Z offset
steps.instruction: Duplicate the Full_Plate target, name it Full_Plate_SlidePickup, and set its Z Position to approximately 29000 (adjust by moving the nozzle to Slides_MetalHolder and inching down until just off the slide surface).

steps.title: Test slide droplet placement
steps.instruction: Select target area Full_Plate and run SpotRun. Load the field file System_setup > Setup_slide_all.fld. Verify droplets appear in the four corners of each slide; adjust slide‑spacing parameter if needed and apply the change to all field files.

steps.title: Gather consumables and nozzles
steps.instruction: Obtain two Scienion PDC nozzles (medium glass for cells, PDC‑70 type‑2 for organic solvents) and H1 fluorocarbon‑coated glass slides. Also have DMSO, 1 M TEAB, Trypsin Gold, Benzonase, DDM, HEPES pH 8.5, labeling reagents (TMT or mTRAQ), and TEAB for mTRAQ.

steps.title: Flush and clean nozzles
steps.instruction: Attach the syringe to each nozzle. Sonicate water and pull it through the nozzle for ~5 min, then pull 100 % ethanol for 1 min, followed by water for 1 min. Avoid wetting the black ring of the PDC.

steps.title: Prepare cell pellets and lyse
steps.instruction: Collect at least 500 000 cells per cell type. Add 100 % DMSO to reach 6000 cells/µL, incubate 20 min for lysis, then add MS‑grade water to dilute to 2000 cells/µL.

steps.title: Add enzymes and overnight digest
steps.instruction: Add 1× Benzonase, 100 mM TEAB, and 20 ng/µL Trypsin Gold to the lysate. Digest overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: Label carrier and reference samples
steps.instruction: Label carrier and reference with the chosen tags, then dilute the combined carrier to 200 cells/µL and the reference to 5 cells/µL.

steps.title: Start CellenONE with two nozzles
steps.instruction: Attach a medium glass PDC nozzle in the far‑left slot and a medium PDC‑70 type‑2 nozzle in the adjacent right slot.

steps.title: Load slides and 384‑well plate
steps.instruction: Place the glass slide holder with H1 slides into the target spotting location. Load a 384‑well plate containing reagents into the probe location, set the probe location to this plate, and set the target location to Full_plate.

steps.title: Prepare cell suspension in PBS
steps.instruction: Suspend cells in 1× PBS at 200–300 cells/µL. If clumping occurs, filter through a 40 µm filter before loading.

steps.title: Load DMSO droplets onto slides
steps.instruction: Load 20 µL of 100 % MS‑grade DMSO into wells D1–D8 (or the required wells) of the 384‑well plate. Load the DMSO_L field file, set Run to Sample_pickup_and_dispense, and execute. Verify droplet placement in the run images; if droplets deviate, wipe with a KimWipe, flip the slide, and re‑dispense.

steps.title: Set humidity for DMSO stability
steps.instruction: Turn the humidifier on, maintain 70 % relative humidity, and set plate temperature to 19 °C (adjust to ~18.5 °C if needed) for the duration of cell dispensing (up to ~2 h).

steps.title: Load cell field file and adjust spots
steps.instruction: Load the Cells field file. For multiple cell suspensions, remove a subset of spots from each cluster to ensure representation of all cell types; leave some empty spots as negative controls. Prepare separate field files for each cell type beforehand.

steps.title: Dispense cells for each type
steps.instruction: Set Run to CellenONE_Basic. Aspirate 10–20 µL of the cell suspension with the left glass nozzle and dispense the first cell type. Repeat aspiration and dispensing for each additional cell type.

steps.title: Adjust humidity after dispensing
steps.instruction: After cell dispensing, set humidity to 75 % RH and cooling to “dew point chase” with a –1 °C deviation (adjust to –1.2 °C at ~19 °C room temperature or –0.75 °C at ~24–25 °C).

steps.title: Dispense water perimeter and start digestion
steps.instruction: Change Run to SpotRun, load the perimeter field file, and dispense system water around each slide to control local evaporation. Then proceed to digestion preparation.

steps.title: Prepare trypsin master mix
steps.instruction: Make 60 µL of master mix containing Trypsin Gold 100 ng/µL, 5 mM HEPES, 0.1 mM DDM, and 0.5× Benzonase. Store in a 1.5 mL tube.

steps.title: Optional degas trypsin solution
steps.instruction: Place the trypsin tube on ice in a styrofoam container filled with ice. Attach the vacuum attachment used for degassing CellenONE water, turn on vacuum, and degas for 10 min.

steps.title: Aspirate master mix into nozzle
steps.instruction: Fill three wells of the 384‑well plate with 30 µL master mix each. Use the Take_20uL_sample task (Nozzle Setup → Do Task) with the type‑2 nozzle to aspirate 20 µL three consecutive times, delivering a total of 60 µL into the nozzle. Perform a dip‑wash immediately after aspiration.

steps.title: Dispense master mix and digest 4 h
steps.instruction: Set Run file to SpotRun_ImageField and load the Digest field file. Dispense the master mix onto each cell droplet. Incubate for 4 hours at room temperature (monitor remotely if desired).

steps.title: Replenish perimeter water during digestion
steps.instruction: Reload the Perimeter field file 1–2 times with system water as needed to prevent evaporation.

steps.title: Dry peptides after digestion pause
steps.instruction: Turn off humidity and cooling, wait ~15 min for single‑cell peptides to dry on the slide. This is a pause point; labeling can be performed the next day.

steps.title: Prepare labeling conditions
steps.instruction: For mTRAQ, load the TEAB field file and dispense 200 mM TEAB to each spot (aspirate 20 µL three times = 60 µL in the nozzle, then spot). Keep humidity at 75 % RH and cooling at –1 °C as used during digestion. For TMT, no humidity or cooling is required.

steps.title: Load label reagents onto plate
steps.instruction: TMT: load all 14 TMT labels into wells G1–G14. mTRAQ 2‑plex: load D0 in G1, D4 in G2, repeat the pair three more times to G8. mTRAQ 3‑plex: load D0 in G1, D4 in G2, D8 in G3, repeat the triplet three more times to G12.

steps.title: Perform labeling dispense and verify droplets
steps.instruction: Load the field file for the first label, set Run method to SamplePickup_And_Dispense, and execute labeling. Turn on the light (light‑bulb button) to check for residual DMSO on the tip; if present, pause, dab tip with a KimWipe, and resume. Verify droplet stream before and after each dispense.

steps.title: Restore humidity for labeling
steps.instruction: Turn humidity and cooling back to the previous digest settings (75 % RH, –1 °C dew‑point chase).

steps.title: Quench with hydroxylamine (first)
steps.instruction: Prepare 5 % hydroxylamine (HA) in MS‑grade water. Load the HA field file, place 30 µL HA into two wells of the 384‑well plate, aspirate 40 µL HA by taking 20 µL from each well, dispense onto the slide, and incubate 20 min.

steps.title: Quench with hydroxylamine (second)
steps.instruction: Repeat the HA dispensing and 20‑minute incubation for the second quenching step.

steps.title: Prepare carrier/references in plates
steps.instruction: Pipette the desired carrier amount diluted in 2 µL of combined carrier‑reference into all wells of the 384‑well plate(s). For 2/3‑plex plexDIA use two plates. If no carrier is used, fill every well with 2 µL MS‑grade water.

steps.title: Pickup samples from slide to plate
steps.instruction: Change target substrate to FullPlate_SamplePickup, set Run to Pickup_off_Slide (or Pickup_off_Slide_smallVol for LF/2‑3‑plex). Load the field file “pickup”; for 2/3‑plex also load “pickup2” and swap the 384‑well plate halfway through.

steps.title: Set up wash tray with ACN/water
steps.instruction: Use a polypropylene container (3.26" × 2.12" × 0.7") with a sticky‑foil cover and a slit for nozzle entry. Fill with 40 mL of 50 % acetonitrile / 50 % MS‑grade water.

steps.title: Run sample pickup method
steps.instruction: Execute the Sample pickup method, watching the first few pickups for proper droplet formation. For 2/3‑plex, change the 384‑well plate and rerun the method after ~2 hours.

steps.title: SpeedVac dry samples and store
steps.instruction: Dry each collected sample in a SpeedVac for 30 minutes to remove residual DMSO, then store at –80 °C until LC/MS analysis.

steps.title: Incubate labeled cells 1 h
steps.instruction: After the final label dispense, allow the cells to react for 1 hour before downstream processing.

steps.title: Resuspend samples for LC/MS
steps.instruction: When ready for LC/MS, resuspend each dried sample in the desired volume of 0.1 % formic acid.
